data.title: C.H. Robinson Secures Up to $500 Million for RXO Acquisition Financing
data.description:
C.H. Robinson entered into a delayed-draw term loan agreement for up to $500 million to help finance its planned acquisition of RXO, with the loan due two years after funding. The company also amended its receivables financing arrangements, including extending a $750 million facility through November 17, 2028 and transferring the administrative agent role to Wells Fargo. Related documents include an amended performance guaranty and an amendment to the receivables sale agreement.

Agreement 1: C.H. Robinson Secures Up to $500 Million for RXO Acquisition Financing

  • Agreement type: Senior unsecured delayed-draw term loan facility
  • Counterparty: U.S. Bank and other lenders
  • Signed / Effective: Nov 19 2026 / same
  • Duration / Termination: Matures two years after funding; commitments expire under specified conditions if undrawn
  • Reason: Help finance the RXO acquisition and related expenses

Agreement 2: C.H. Robinson Extends $750 Million Receivables Facility Through 2028

  • Agreement type: Seventh amendment to receivables purchase agreement
  • Counterparty: Bank of America and Wells Fargo
  • Signed / Effective: Nov 18 2026 / same
  • Duration / Termination: Scheduled purchase termination date of Nov 17 2028
  • Reason: Continue and extend the company's receivables financing facility

Agreement 3: C.H. Robinson Updates Performance Guaranty for Receivables Facility

  • Agreement type: Amended and restated performance guaranty
  • Counterparty: Wells Fargo
  • Signed / Effective: Nov 18 2026 / same
  • Reason: Support the amended receivables financing arrangements

Agreement 4: C.H. Robinson Amends Receivables Sale Agreement Alongside Facility Changes

  • Agreement type: Second amendment to receivables sale agreement
  • Counterparty: C.H. Robinson Receivables and the originators
  • Signed / Effective: Nov 18 2026 / same
  • Reason: Make related changes to the receivables financing structure

data.description:
RNS Number : 1177E Smarter Web Company PLC (The) 20 November 2026  

20 November 2026

The Smarter Web Company PLC

(“The Smarter Web Company” or the "Company")

PDMR/Director Dealing

The Smarter Web Company announces that on 20 November 2026, Andrew Webley, Chief Executive Officer, together with his spouse and children, purchased an aggregate of 148,597 ordinary shares of £0.001 each in the Company (“Ordinary Shares”), for an aggregate cost of £51,510, as detailed in the PDMR Form below.

Following these purchases, Andrew Webley together with his spouse and children are interested in, in aggregate, 27,713,731 Ordinary Shares, representing approximately 7.33 per cent of the Company’s issued Ordinary Share capital.

Enquiries

The Smarter Web Company

CEO / CFO

+44 (0) 207 186 9030

About The Smarter Web Company

The Company owns and operates digital services businesses focused on web design, development and digital marketing. The Company serves more than 500 client websites across a diverse range of sectors and generates a significant and growing proportion of its revenue through long-term client relationships and retained service arrangements.

The Company's strategy combines the operation and acquisition of cash-generative businesses with a Bitcoin treasury policy designed to build long-term Shareholder value (the "Bitcoin Treasury Policy"). The Directors believe that Bitcoin will form a significant part of the future global financial system and have therefore adopted this Bitcoin Treasury Policy under which Bitcoin is the Company's primary treasury reserve asset.

The primary objectives of the Bitcoin Treasury Policy are to support the Company's overall capital position and to seek to increase Bitcoin per Ordinary Share over time, with a secondary objective of increasing the total number of Bitcoin held on the Company's balance sheet. The Directors believe that growing Bitcoin per share while simultaneously increasing the scale of the Company's Bitcoin holdings creates a stronger balance sheet and supports the Company as a whole in providing a more attractive investment proposition for existing and prospective Shareholders.

As the strength of the balance sheet increases, the Company believes it can access larger pools of capital on favourable terms, provided such capital raising activity remains accretive to Bitcoin per Ordinary Share. This creates a cycle in which capital can be deployed to pursue strategic acquisitions and acquire additional Bitcoin that strengthen the Company's operating businesses, increase revenues and cash generation, and further enhance the overall strength of the Company.

The Ordinary Shares are admitted to listing on the equity shares (commercial companies) category of the Official List and to trading on the Main Market of the London Stock Exchange under the ticker SWC and are quoted on the OTCQB Venture Market in the U.S. under the ticker TSWCF. The Ordinary Shares can also be traded on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange under the ticker 3M8.

The Preferred Shares are admitted to listing on the non-equity shares and non-voting equity shares category of the Official List and to trading on the Main Market of the London Stock Exchange under the ticker MORE and are quoted on the OTCQB Venture Market in the U.S. under the ticker MORPF.

Please also see "The 10 Year Plan", announced by the Company via a regulatory information service at 7.00 a.m. on 28 April 2025 and available on the Company's website: https://www.smarterwebcompany.co.uk

Follow the Company on X: https://x.com/smarterwebuk

The Smarter Web Company's Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) is 213800VQO9FUG4PZMP73.

The Directors of the Company accept responsibility for the contents of this announcement.

Important Notice

The Smarter Web Company PLC holds treasury reserves and surplus cash in Bitcoin. Bitcoin is a type of cryptocurrency or cryptoasset. Whilst the Board of Directors of the Company considers holding Bitcoin to be in the best interests of the Company, the Board remains aware that the financial regulator in the UK (the Financial Conduct Authority or FCA) considers investment in Bitcoin to be high risk. An investment in the Company is not an investment in Bitcoin, either directly or by proxy. However, the Board of Directors of the Company considers Bitcoin to be an appropriate store of value and growth for the Company's reserves and, accordingly, the Company is materially exposed to Bitcoin. Such an approach is innovative, and the Board of Directors of the Company wishes to be clear and transparent with prospective and actual investors in the Company on the Company's position in this regard.

The Company is neither authorised nor regulated in the conduct of its business by the FCA, and there is currently limited regulation of cryptocurrencies (such as Bitcoin) in the UK. As with most other investments, the value of Bitcoin can go down as well as up, and therefore the value of the Company's Bitcoin holdings can fluctuate. The Company may not be able to realise its Bitcoin exposure for the same as it paid in the first place or even for the value the Company ascribes to its Bitcoin positions due to these market movements. An investment in the Company is not protected by the UK's Financial Ombudsman Service or the Financial Services Compensation Scheme.

Nevertheless, the Board of Directors of the Company has taken the decision to invest in Bitcoin, and in doing so is mindful of the special risks Bitcoin presents to the Company's financial position. These risks include (but are not limited to): (i) the value of Bitcoin can be highly volatile, with value dropping as quickly as it can rise. Investors in Bitcoin must be prepared to lose all money invested in Bitcoin; (ii) the Bitcoin market is largely unregulated. There is a risk of losing money due to risks such as cyber-attacks, financial crime and counterparty failure; (iii) the Company may not be able to buy or sell its Bitcoin at will. The ability to buy or sell Bitcoin depends on various factors, including the supply and demand in the market at the relevant time. Operational failings such as technology outages, cyber-attacks and comingling of funds could cause unwanted delay; and (iv) cryptoassets are characterised in some quarters by high degrees of fraud, money laundering and financial crime. In addition, there is a perception in some quarters that cyber-attacks are prominent, which can lead to theft of holdings or ransom demands. The Board of Directors of the Company does not subscribe to such a negative view, especially in relation to Bitcoin. However, prospective investors in the Company are encouraged to do their own research before investing.

data.title: Krista Rogalski Elevated To Director, Technology Talent Acquisition At Disney
data.description:
Rogalski Steps Into The Role After More Than A Decade At Disney, With Experience Across Technology Recruitment, Hiring Strategy And Talent Leadership

The Walt Disney Company has elevated Krista Rogalski to Director, Technology Talent Acquisition (IA), effective October 2026. Rogalski brings more than a decade of experience at the company, having progressed through multiple roles in technology recruitment and talent acquisition leadership.

From Sourcing To Leadership

Rogalski joined Disney in December 2015 as a Technical Talent Sourcer. She subsequently served as Technical Recruiter, Senior Technical Recruiter, Manager, Technical Talent Acquisition and Senior Manager, Technology Talent Acquisition before taking up her current position.

In her most recent role, which she held from May 2022 to October 2026, Rogalski led talent acquisition teams supporting technology, media and other business functions. Her responsibilities included aligning recruitment strategies with business priorities, developing recruiting managers and improving hiring processes.

Focus On Hiring Strategy

As Senior Manager, Rogalski worked with senior business and human resources leaders to assess workforce requirements and establish recruiting priorities. She also focused on interview standardisation, candidate assessment, recruiter development and the use of recruitment data to inform decisions.

Her work included evaluating recruiting operating models and improving collaboration across talent acquisition and human resources teams to respond to changing business requirements.

Experience Beyond Disney

Before joining Disney, Rogalski worked at Kforce Inc., where she held Technical Recruiter and Technology VMO Recruiter positions between March 2014 and December 2015.

She previously spent more than five years at Bridgewater Associates, working in technology recruiting and project management from November 2008 to December 2013. Earlier in her career, she served as a Diversity Specialist at Panasonic between July 2002 and August 2008.

Education And Expertise

Rogalski holds a bachelor's degree in Business Administration, with a specialisation in Management, from William Paterson University of New Jersey.

Her career spans technology recruitment, recruiting operations, team development and workforce planning. In her new role, she brings experience in aligning talent acquisition practices with business needs and managing recruitment teams across multiple functions.

data.title: Apollo Hospitals Hits Record High As Macquarie Double Upgrades Stock, Sees 20% Upside
data.description:
Shares of Apollo Hospitals surged more than 5 per cent to a fresh all-time high on Friday after global brokerage Macquarie upgraded the stock by two notches and sharply raised its target price, citing improving earnings prospects, easing valuation concerns and healthy capacity expansion.

Macquarie upgraded Apollo Hospitals to ‘Outperform’ from ‘Underperform’ and increased its price target to Rs 10,500 from Rs 6,230, indicating a potential upside of 20.2 per cent from Thursday’s closing price.

The brokerage believes consensus earnings estimates have bottomed out, while the stock’s valuations have become more reasonable. It also noted that the initial profitability pressure associated with the hospital operator’s bed expansion programme is largely reflected in expectations, with newly added capacity witnessing a healthy ramp-up.

The upgrade follows Apollo Hospitals’ stronger-than-expected performance in the September quarter, when both revenue and profit surpassed market estimates.

Q2 Earnings Beat Street Expectations

Apollo Hospitals reported a 33.6 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 660 crore, exceeding analysts’ expectations of Rs 632 crore.

Revenue grew 23 per cent to Rs 7,615 crore from Rs 6,189 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, ahead of the Street estimate of Rs 7,515 crore.

Operating performance also improved, with earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) rising 28.8 per cent to Rs 1,191 crore from Rs 925 crore a year earlier. The figure was above the market estimate of Rs 1,160 crore.

EBITDA margin expanded to 15.6 per cent from 14.9 per cent in the year-ago period, surpassing analysts’ expectations of 15.4 per cent.

The hospital operator also reported stronger operational metrics. Occupancy improved to 73 per cent from 69 per cent a year earlier, while inpatient volumes increased 14 per cent. Average revenue per occupied bed rose 8 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1,86,880.

Stock Extends Gains For Second Consecutive Month

Apollo Hospitals shares climbed as much as 5.3 per cent to touch a record high of Rs 9,205 during Friday’s session. The stock subsequently pared some gains and was trading 4.6 per cent higher at Rs 9,138.

The rally has extended the stock’s November gains to around 8 per cent, following a 3.5 per cent rise in October. This marks its strongest monthly performance since February 2026, when the shares advanced 12.4 per cent.

Apollo Hospitals has recorded gains in seven of the 11 months of 2026 so far, with its year-to-date return reaching 28.5 per cent.

data.title: Portugal's Santander Totta focused on organic growth, not acquisitions
data.description:
Santander Totta, Portugal's third-largest bank and owned by Spain's Santander , remains focused on organic growth rather than acquisitions, CEO Isabel Guerreiro said on Friday, amid talk of further consolidation in the country's banking sector.

  • Renewed focus on sector consolidation has been fuelled by uncertainty surrounding the future ownership of Millennium bcp, Portugal's largest listed bank

  • Reuters reported in March 2024 that China's Fosun was open to selling its remaining stake in Millennium bcp following the disposal of a 5.6% holding earlier that year

  • Fosun is the largest single shareholder in Millennium bcp, with a stake of about 20%

  • Without referring to Millennium bcp, Guerreiro said at a conference hosted by business daily Jornal de Negocios that her strategy was to pursue organic growth, adding that she had no visibility on whether there was room for further consolidation

  • The CEO said Santander Totta wanted to continue to grow and attract clients through its value proposition, adding that Portuguese banking was "frankly good ... and has little to learn from other markets"

data.title: SocGen sees S&P 500 ending 2027 at 8,500 on AI, earnings support
data.description:
Societe Generale expects the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX to rise to 8,500 by the end of 2027, driven by continued support from AI-related investments and resilient corporate earnings.

The target implies an upside of about 18.5% from Thursday's close of 7,175.83.

  • SocGen said 2027 should mark the end of de-rating and the start of re-rating for the S&P 500, as it expects two more quarter-point rate hikes from the US Fed

  • The French bank expects the Fed to deliver the final rate hike in March 2027, a move it says should trigger a market re-rating phase, with the strongest returns coming in the second quarter

  • The bank maintained its 2027 earnings expectations for the S&P 500 at 11%

  • For Europe, SocGen forecasts the STOXX 600 index to reach 720 by the end of 2027

  • "A renewed rotation of global capital towards Europe could provide an early-year tailwind, reinforced by the positive seasonality seen in recent years," SocGen said

  • It added that investors should maintain high equity exposure, citing continued support from AI adoption, productivity gains and earnings growth

data.title: Anthropic's stock slides closer to IPO price and drags down the AI trade
data.description:
By Emily Bary

Anthropic's inability to hold its opening stock price has been seen as 'bad for the rest of tech'

Anthropic finished with a $1.29 trillion valuation on Thursday.

There was no honeymoon period for Anthropic after its record-breaking initial public offering.

Shares of the AI company are down 9% in premarket action on Friday and on pace for a gloomy second day of trading. On a premarket basis, Anthropic's stock (ANT) is at $87.43, well below its $111.50 opening price, and falling closer toward its $83 IPO price.

It's a downbeat sign for the broader technology ecosystem as well, with AI stocks taking a beating across the board. Among the biggest losers are shares of Sandisk (SNDK), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Dell Technologies (DELL), Nebius Group (NBIS) and Arm Holdings (ARM).

"The vast majority of this continued selling pressure in the last 24 hours feels more to do with" the Anthropic IPO than it does with some less-than-perfect earnings reports in the technology sector, according to Jefferies trading-desk analyst Jeffrey Favuzza.

He wrote in a note to clients that Anthropic's inability to hold its opening price and the downward pressure in Friday's premarket action is being viewed as "bad for the rest of tech."

Anthropic's IPO was seen as a tentpole event for the AI trade. The company finished with a $1.29 trillion valuation on Thursday, according to Dow Jones Market Data, and premarket levels Friday would translate to a market capitalization of about $1.16 trillion.

Some analysts initiated coverage of Anthropic's stock after Thursday's close, chiming in with mixed views.

"We are cautious, not negative," wrote Seaport Research's Jay Goldberg, who launched coverage of shares with a neutral rating.

He called Anthropic an "incredible company," but also one "asking for an incredible leap of faith by investors."

"We think the company will need time to grow into its valuation and answer some very big questions about its growth trajectory," he continued. For instance, the company saw 43% revenue growth from the second quarter to the third quarter. That compared with a much faster 144% growth rate from the first quarter to the second quarter.

Goldberg referred to that as a "worrying" deceleration. "To merit its valuation, it will need to see much higher growth rates over the next two years," he added.

William Blair's Arjun Bhatia was more upbeat, calling Anthropic a "generational company driving a generational technology shift" as he began his own coverage of the stock with an outperform rating.

"Questions about the future are worth asking, even those that don't have an answer at this point," he wrote.

But at the same time, he and his team "don't want to miss the forest for the trees."

"We think AI is a generational shift in the tech landscape, and Anthropic is leading the charge in developing AI with a select handful of other companies," Bhatia wrote. "Over the next decade, we think Anthropic is only going to become more important and consume a greater portion of enterprise spend," meaning it will command more of the budget that businesses have to allocate toward technology.

-Emily Bary
